n0: Swarm detail two. Read the cockpit. Five agents talking at once is noise, unless you can see who's doing what.
n1: So every agent gets a face on the live card. A double ring is the lead, a dashed plus an open seat. A bright ring is on a turn, an amber dot has messages waiting, and a faded face is idle.
n2: This is a Crew: a lead, up to four workers, and a ten dollar ceiling.
n3: The question is whether a five person team should split billing out of its Rails monolith. The lead takes the first turn, then fills its four seats.
n4: Security and the cost skeptic wear amber dots: the lead addressed them, so their turns are queued. When the lead's turn ends, its face fades. Idle costs nothing.
n5: Then a worker's answer names the lead. An amber dot lands, and the lead lights up for its next turn.
n6: Beside the faces, four meters run toward the plan's ceilings: turns, time, fresh tokens, and cost, with the burn rate per minute.
n7: The Map tab draws who addressed whom. The lead fans out to every worker, and the crossings are workers challenging each other.
n8: A minute and a half in, the lead concludes. The outcome stays on top: keep billing in the monolith, and draw the boundary inside Rails.
n9: Spend splits the sixty four cents by agent. Produced holds the report.
n10: Activity is every turn and how long it took. About keeps the task and the transcript. And Agents gives each one's role, turns and cost.
n11: The channel is the record. The cockpit is what you check at a glance: who's working, who's waiting, and what it's costing.
n12: Next, how big a crew a question needs.
n13: Keelson. Lay the keel, raise the ribs.
